extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO patent examiners (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing filing, oath/declaration, specification/drawings, incorporation by reference, inventorship, publication, and prosecution of continuation, divisional, and continuation-in-part applications under 37 CFR 1.53(b) and 37 CFR 1.63(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing requirements under 37 CFR 1.53(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an application filed under this section is the date on which a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 containing a description pursuant to § 1.71 and at least one claim pursuant to § 1.75, and any drawing required by § 1.81(a) are filed in the Patent and Trademark Office. No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing fee and an oath/declaration are required by 37 CFR 1.51(b) for a complete application but may be filed after the filing date upon payment of the surcharge in 37 CFR 1.16(f). 37 CFR 1.53(b) is the default application rule (exceptions: national stage 1.495, provisional 1.53(c), CPA design 1.53(d)). A continuing application may be filed under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) and 37 CFR 1.78(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of continuing applications and filing paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A continuation or divisional application that names as inventors the same or fewer than all of the inventors named in the prior application may be filed under this paragraph or paragraph (d) of this section. (2) A continuation-in-part application or a continuation or divisional naming an inventor not named in the prior application must be filed under this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish continuation, divisional, and CIP based on whether new matter is added or whether a new inventor is named. Choose correct paragraph to avoid improper application treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a newly executed oath or declaration is not required (37 CFR 1.63(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration is not required in a continuation or divisional application, provided that: (i) The prior nonprovisional application contained an oath/declaration as prescribed; (ii) The continuation/divisional was filed by all or by fewer than all inventors named in the prior application; (iii) The specification and drawings in the continuation/divisional contain no matter that would have been new matter in the prior application; and (iv) A copy of the executed oath/declaration filed in the prior application, showing the signature or an indication thereon that it was signed, is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy must show signature or indication (e.g., '/s/'). If one or more inventors are added, or if the continuing application contains matter that would have been new in the prior application, a newly executed oath/declaration is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of executed oath/declaration: submission and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: When a copy of an oath or declaration from a prior application is filed in a continuation or divisional application under 37 CFR 1.53(b), special care should be taken to ensure that the copy is matched with the correct application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the copy with a cover letter explaining the intended application or include an adhesive label stating the target application number. Do not rely solely on the cover letter because attachments may be separated during processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when copy of prior oath/declaration involves 1.47 status
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the executed oath/declaration copy submitted was originally filed in a prior application accorded status under § 1.47, the copy must be accompanied by a copy of the decision granting petition to accord § 1.47 status unless all inventors/legal representatives have filed an oath/declaration to join in an application accorded § 1.47 status of which the continuation/divisional claims benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If nonsigning inventors later join, submit copies of subsequently executed oaths/declarations. Applications with such copies and a 1.47 decision should be forwarded to the Office of Petitions; Rule 47 notification procedures follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a newly executed oath/declaration is required
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration must be filed in a continuation or divisional application naming an inventor not named in the prior application. A newly executed oath or declaration is also required in a continuation-in-part application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all inventors sign when new inventors are named. Newly executed oath must be in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 and signed by all inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and drawings: no new matter and filing options
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application may be filed by providing: (A) a new specification and drawings and a copy of the signed oath/declaration as filed in the prior application provided the new specification and drawings do not contain subject matter that would have been new matter; or (B) a new specification and drawings and a newly executed oath/declaration provided the new specification and drawings do not contain subject matter that would have been new matter in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is responsible to review new specification/drawings to ensure no new matter. If questionable, file with a newly executed oath/declaration. If new matter is present after a copy-of-oath filing, examiner should notify applicant and require a new oath/declaration and redesignation as a continuation-in-part; form paragraph 2.10.01 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended practice for claims and preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should file a new set of claims as the original claims of the continuing application instead of filing a copy of the claims from the prior application and a preliminary amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments present on the filing date are part of the original disclosure, but preliminary amendments may not be reflected in the published application unless also submitted through the EFS. To have a publication contain only desired claims, file the continuation/divisional with a new specification containing only the desired set of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication considerations for continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any utility or plant patent application that will be published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b) should be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) with a specification (including the claims) and drawings that the applicant would like to have published because the Office will generally publish the specification (including the claims) and drawings as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments may not be reflected in the patent application publication unless the amended specification is also submitted via EFS. Filing a continuation with a new specification containing the desired claims is strongly recommended to control what is published and to preserve potential provisional rights under 35 U.S.C. 154(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference rules (37 CFR 1.57 and 1.78)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may incorporate by reference a prior application by including an explicit statement in the specification that specifically enumerated prior application(s) are 'hereby incorporated by reference.' For applications filed on or after September 21, 2004, a claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78 is considered an incorporation by reference as to inadvertently omitted material subject to 37 CFR 1.57(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For apps filed on/after Sept 21, 2004, applicants are encouraged to provide an explicit incorporation by reference statement. An incorporation by reference statement added after filing is not effective because no new matter can be added after the filing date. Mere reference to another application/publication is not an incorporation for 35 U.S.C. 112 purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application NOT entitled to a filing date when material omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Material needed to accord an application a filing date may not be incorporated by reference unless an appropriate petition under 37 CFR 1.57(a)(3) or 37 CFR 1.182 is granted. Until such petition is granted, the application will not be entitled to a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Sept 21, 2004, if material needed for a filing date is completely contained in a prior-filed application to which benefit is claimed, applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.57(a)(3) with fee 1.17(f) and an amendment with omitted material requesting entry and accord of the original deposit filing date. A petition under 1.182 and fee may also be used where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application entitled to a filing date despite inadvertent omission
rubrics_metrics.description: If a continuation/divisional originally filed on/after Sept 21, 2004 does not include an explicit incorporation by reference statement and is entitled to a filing date despite inadvertent omission, applicant may be permitted to add the omitted material by amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments must be made within any time period set by the Office. If the original filing included a proper explicit incorporation by reference, omitted pages or figures may be added by amendment provided the omitted items contain only matter in common with a properly incorporated document. Submit amendments prior to first Office action to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship handling in continuation/divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of a continuation or divisional application by all or by fewer than all inventors named in a prior application without a newly executed oath/declaration is permitted. Applicant may (A) file a newly executed oath/declaration signed by the inventors, or (B) file a copy of the prior oath/declaration accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of names of persons who are not inventors in the continuation/divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a continuation/divisional is filed with a copy of a prior oath/declaration but without a deletion statement signed by an authorized person, the continuation/divisional will be treated as naming the persons named in the copy as inventors. Deletion statements must be signed by those authorized under 37 CFR 1.33(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 47 processing for applications with 1.47 status
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.63(d)(3) requires copies of decisions granting petitions to accord 37 CFR 1.47 status when the executed oath/declaration of which a copy is submitted was originally filed in a prior application accorded § 1.47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New continuation/divisional apps filed under 1.53(b) that contain a copy of an oath/declaration not signed by an inventor and a copy of the 1.47 decision should be forwarded by OIPE to the Office of Petitions. The Office of Petitions will mail a letter stating 'Rule 47' status has been accorded to the continuation/divisional but will not repeat the notice to the nonsigning inventor nor the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of attorney or correspondence address identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the power of attorney or correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, the change in power of attorney or correspondence address must be identified in the continuation or divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise the Office may not recognize the change of power of attorney or correspondence address in the continuation/divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity status assertion for continuation/divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: If small entity status has been established in a parent application and is still proper and desired in a continuation or divisional application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), a new assertion as to the continued entitlement to small entity status under 37 CFR 1.27 is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 509.03 for details on asserting and documenting small entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits or declarations from prior application do not automatically carry over
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations, such as those submitted under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131 and 1.132 filed during prosecution of the prior nonprovisional application do not automatically become a part of a continuation or divisional application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where it is desired to rely on an earlier filed affidavit or declaration, the applicant should make such remarks of record in the 1.53(b) application and include a copy of the original affidavit/declaration. Use form paragraph 2.03 (provided) for instructions to applicant. Do not use form paragraph 2.03 in 1.53(d) applications because such affidavits do automatically become part of 1.53(d) applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time when establishing continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extension of time is necessary to establish continuity between the prior application and the continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the petition for an extension of time must be filed as a separate paper directed to the prior nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3) an authorization to charge all required fees will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time in any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition. A petition for extension directed to the prior application must be accompanied by its own certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 or 1.10 if those rules' benefits are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment of the prior nonprovisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.53(b) and 1.63(d) practice, the prior nonprovisional application is not automatically abandoned upon filing of the continuing application. If the prior application is to be expressly abandoned, such a paper must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.138.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior application has a notice of allowance, it can become abandoned by nonpayment of the issue fee. If an issue fee has been paid, a petition to withdraw the prior application from issue must be filed before it can be abandoned (37 CFR 1.313). If the prior application is before the Board, forward a separate notice to the Board. Termination after CAFC mandate noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination practice and preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice relating to making first action rejections final also applies to continuation and divisional applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Any preliminary amendment present on the filing date of an application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) is part of the original disclosure. Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., complete claim listing whenever a claim is added, canceled, or amended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should file a new set of claims as original claims rather than relying on preliminary amendments. Examiners should classify and assign Technology Center taking into consideration the claims that will be before the examiner upon entry of a preliminary amendment. See MPEP §§ 706.07(b), 714, and 607 for related practice.
